3. The cases before me are unique cases of forgery. Allottees, 3 in number are of same name, same parentage, similiar hand writings with similiar apparently same documents but 3 persons claiming the plot of RAJUK of them one must be genuine with original papers and others are not. I have taken a strong heavy burden to single out that genuine person with original documents. 

 25. Learned Advocate relied on number of decisions, on question of burden of proof of documents 4 BLC (AD) 191, 39 DLR (AD) 237, burden of proof of transaction, AIR 2000 (SC) 1203, 3 SCC 2000, 312, on status of titleless person, 61 DLR (AD) 116, on adverse posses sion, 11 MLR (AD)151, on power of appellate Court in deciding the suit finally instead of sending it on remand, 9 MLR (AD) 169, 4 MLR (AD) 1, 11 MLR (AD)119, on verification of signatures, 56 DLR (AD)117, DLR (AD) 117, on unspecified suit land , 12 MLR (AD) 105, 31 DLR (AD) 219, on evidence beyond pleadings, 38 DLR 39, on maintainability of the suit for simple declaration 16 DLR 272, 46 DLR (AD) 148, 2 XP (AD) 194, on adaption of deposition, AIR 1966 (SC) 1072 and on institution of criminal proceeding for using forged document 14 MLR (AD) 52-55. 

 42. To hold a bainapatra good prime factor is to prove passing of consideration. It appears that defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) who plaintiff later on accepted as heirs of defendant No.1, these defendants did not subscribe to the contention of the plaintiff in the, matter execution of bainama by Samsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Baro Mogbazar as such it is plaintiff sole burden to prove whether consideration money was passed or not. In these respect plaintiff examined himself as PW 1, MA Hashem, PW 2, Md. Sadrul Huda and PW 3, Hasan Imam Chowdhury, Mr. Fida M Kamal, learned Advocate submits that these 3 witnesses univocally stated earnest money was paid. Let us consider the deposition of PW 1, MA Hashem who in his deposition stated that: 

 74. The submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellants are of no substance as from the facts of Title Suit No.51 of-2004, it appears that plaintiffs of the instant suit filed written statement as heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Baro Mogbazar, not of Mirpur and it appears that after the death of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Baro Moghbazar on 2-2-2004, MA Hashem filed the aforesaid suit on 8-4-2004 against Shamsul Kabir Huniayun Reza of Mirpur, Dhaka and also that summons were served and received by Shamsul Kabir Huamyun Reza of Mirpur long after 3 months of the institution of the suit by signing his name and in his own signature. Moreover, MA Hashem in his suit accepted, as it appears Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Baro Mogbazar, when he has no alternative as original allottee of the suit property appeared in Court and it will be heavy burden on his part to continue (i.e chale-e-nea) Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur as original Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Baro Moghbazar, M.A Hashem accepted the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Baro Moghbazar as such it cannot be definitely said this defendant No. 2 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza is dead person and same Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Baro Mogh bazar. MA Hashem did not resolve this dispute. And next point that since Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza already dead he should not be impleaded as defendant in the instant suit. In answering it may be said that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur is dead person is in the pocket of MA Hashem not in the record of the suit. It is on record that Shamsul Kabir Humayn Reza of 157, Baro Moghbazar is dead person who is not defendant. Other question raised by Mr. Fida M. Kamal that Eastern Housing Ltd. should not be a party to the suit as Eastern Housing Ltd. represented the plaintiffs as power of attorney holder. To answer this point it may be said that Eastern Housing Ltd. has been made proforma-defendant as it has a case of itself besides power of attorney holder of the plaintiffs. Moreover, as per Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure no suit can be dismissed on the ground misjoinder of parties even if the submission of the learned Advocate be accepted as such. 

 76. In civil proceeding as per seciton 101 of the evidence Act the burden to prove the case of a party in a suit is entirely dependant upon him at his own risk. If any party is not interested to prove his case, the Court cannot make him bound to prove his case. Here in these three suits since the material issue for decision arisen as to the identity of the real Reza and real lessee all the parties of three suits decided to adopt the evidences given as plaintiff in his suit as evidence of other suit wherein he is a defendant. Accordingly on the application of adoption of each party, the deposition given as plaintif in his own suit has been adopted as deposition of defendant in the other suit with the consent of all the parties. So, the consented party now at the appellate stage cannot raise the question of validity or legality of adoption. Moreover seciton 33 of evidence Act have also empowers the Court to adopt the depositon of one suit as of the deposition of other suit on the consent of the parties involved in the suit. On the other hand, if any plaintiff suit is not desire to adopt his and his witnesses' deposition , as position of D.Ws in other suit wherein he is defendant, but agrued the case without giving evidences it would be al his own risk.
